task: Extend the Narwhal#185 SSH host-key trust fix (accept-new + a real known_hosts file, not StrictHostKeyChecking=no + UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null) beyond scripts/cloud/*.sh to the remaining scripts that still opened SSH connections with the insecure pair

events.summary: Narwhal#185 fixed scripts/cloud/*.sh only (lib-ssh.sh + R151/R151b). A follow-up review found the same StrictHostKeyChecking=no + UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null pair still live in scripts/test/verify-isolation.sh, scripts/test/airgap-isolate-kakao.sh, scripts/test/regression-check-kakao.sh's own runtime setup_ssh(), scripts/airgap/06-configure-mirrors.sh, and scripts/common/set-config.sh
grep -rn 'StrictHostKeyChecking=no' scripts/ | grep 'UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null' found the insecure pair live in all five target files before the fix

verify-isolation.sh, airgap-isolate-kakao.sh, and regression-check-kakao.sh's setup_ssh() now source scripts/cloud/lib-ssh.sh and use KAKAO_SSH_OPTS (accept-new pinned against a persistent per-cluster known_hosts file), matching the provision-kakao.sh pattern -- all three already share lib-ssh.sh's TF_DIR/repo-root assumptions. 06-configure-mirrors.sh runs node-to-node with no TF_DIR/terraform state available on that host, so it was adapted minimally to StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new against the node's own default known_hosts instead of forcing lib-ssh.sh's TF_DIR-based path to fit. set-config.sh targets the local Vagrant cluster (not Kakao), so it pins accept-new against a repo-scoped .vagrant/known_hosts file of its own.

Added R153 (scans the four adapted files plus regression-check-kakao.sh's own setup_ssh() function body for the insecure pair) and R153b (proves R153 catches a reintroduced insecure pair via a sed-mutated copy of verify-isolation.sh) to scripts/test/regression-check-kakao.sh, alongside the existing R152/R152b/R152c cloud-script checks

bash -n on all five touched files passed; shellcheck --severity=warning across the whole scripts/ tree produced no output; ./scripts/test/regression-check-kakao.sh --static ran 203 checks, 0 failures (R152, R152b, R152c, R153, R153b, R151, R151b all PASS)

Repo-wide grep for the insecure pair after the fix found it still present in scripts/up.sh (a Vagrant-only bootstrap script not in the follow-up review's scope), so this change does not close Narwhal#185 outright -- it is referenced from the PR without a closing keyword

All five files named in the follow-up review now fail closed on a changed host key instead of silently trusting it; a static regression check (R153/R153b) guards against the pattern reappearing in any of them

The insecure StrictHostKeyChecking=no + UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null pattern is fixed in every location the follow-up review flagged, with a regression check covering all of them; one unrelated pre-existing instance (scripts/up.sh) remains out of scope and is called out rather than silently left
